It's not so much a conspiracy against Trump as it is trying to patch up our broken electoral system that makes it where a single man deciding to run as an independent or not could decide, with near complete certainty, the result of a presidential election. That said - they're idiots. They could actually be using their influence for positive change for everybody. For instance if the US used an electoral system like instant run off, let alone the proportional systems that the rest of the developed world, nearly in entirety, has swapped to then we wouldn't have these issues.

The way instant run off works is you can vote for a number of candidates in order of preference. Imagine Hillary-Trump-Bush runs and the results are 36-34-30. In our present system Hillary wins. Instant runoff works as we're used to when there are two candidates. When there are more than two candidates it looks at the candidate that received the lowest number of #1 votes. That candidate is then removed and any votes that had him as their #1 now become votes for their #2 candidate. So imagine, for simplicity that 100% of the Trump votes were Trump-Bush votes. So what happens in instant run off is in the first round trump is eliminated since he had the fewest #1 votes. Those 34% of votes that were Trump-Bush tickets now become Bush votes. And Bush now wins the election 64% to 30%.

Everything works exactly like we're used to, except now we don't have the Ross Perot effect of a single man -who himself is not actually terribly likely to be elected- being able to decide the election for another candidate by splitting the vote. It's also amazing from a voter perspective since it takes out the part of voting where you vote for somebody you don't actually want because you're afraid of 'wasting' your vote and think he's more electable than your actual preference. Libertarian republicans could vote Libertarian first and then establishment republican without fear of wasting their votes, green democrats could do the same, and so on.

There are other systems that are even more desirable than instant run off, but our current system -first past the post- is basically without a doubt the most broken electoral system there is. Here are the countries still using first past the post:

Anguilla Antigua and Barbuda Azerbaijan Bahamas Bangladesh Barbados Belize Bermuda Botswana Canada Cook Islands Dominica Ethiopia Gambia Ghana Grenada Isle Of Man India Jamaica Kenya Liberia Madagascar Malawi Malaysia Maldives Micronesia Myanmar Nigeria Pakistan Palau Saint Kitts and Nevis Saint Lucia Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Sierra Leone Singapore Solomon Islands Swaziland Tanzania Tonga Trinidad and Tobago Uganda United Kingdom United States British Virgin Islands Yemen Zambia Zimbabwe

That's some sad list of company we share. I'm happy to at least see some acknowledgement that our electoral system is broken, but putting a bandaid on first past the post is not how you fix it.
